title: The unique bond in a cotree with one tree edge
statement: Let $G$ be a finite connected graph, let $T$ be a spanning tree of $G$, and let $e$ be an edge of $T$. Write $\bar T = E(G) \setminus E(T)$ for the cotree, the set of edges of $G$ that lie outside $T$. Then (i) no bond of $G$ is contained in $\bar T$, and (ii) there is exactly one bond of $G$ contained in $\{e\} \cup \bar T$.
hypotheses_covered: $T$ is a subgraph of $G$ (hence a spanning tree)
